topics.title: Audition Chaos with Five Girls
topics.summary: During a chaotic cable show audition, the host struggles to manage five young women and comedian Dice amidst inappropriate questions about their appearances, an interruption by Dick Clark, and concerns over potential censorship due to audience reactions – ultimately leading to a disorganized mix of interviews and unexpected celebrity encounters.

topics.title: Dice's Chaotic Nassau Coliseum Plans
topics.summary: During a radio show segment, host Howard engages in chaotic conversations with callers Dice Clay and Richard Lewis. The discussion quickly devolves into arguments about personal grievances, including accusations of stealing material and disrupting relationships, alongside bizarre tangents involving tattoos, potential romantic interests, and an attempt to recruit women for a Nassau Coliseum event.

topics.title: Dice Evicts a Comedy Store Tenant – Hypnosis and Confusion
topics.summary: Richard recounts his landlord Dice evicting Karl LeBeau from their Crest Hill rental due to frequent visits to a comedy store and wives/girlfriends, revealing details about other tenants including Mitzi. The conversation spirals into an awkward encounter involving hypnotism and bizarre comments regarding Dick Clark’s behavior at the show.

topics.title: Dice Clay Ticket Dispute
topics.summary: During a radio segment, Howard Stern discusses an issue with dice Clay and his team regarding promised concert tickets. Hot Tub Johnny West, dice’s manager, complicates matters by demanding to speak directly with Howard, leading to disputes over the tickets' distribution and ultimately resulting in Howard refusing any involvement.

topics.title: Radio Host’s Rambling Session
topics.summary: A radio host engages in a lengthy and disorganized conversation with guest Scott Cooper, discussing his respect for the comedian while delving into personal anxieties about money, relationships, bizarre encounters involving ‘hot tub Johnny West,’ and obsessive archiving of NBC memos. The discussion includes references to past shows like Geraldo’s lesbian show and frustration over Eddie Murphy imitating Michael Jackson.” 2 sentences, 54 words.

topics.title: Rapping Fantasies and Gay Newspaper Critique
topics.summary: The broadcast features a man rapping about his desires, referencing Gloria Steinemund and discussing Morton Downey Jr.’s failed television show while analyzing a gay newspaper’s coverage of Stern's opinions. Later, the hosts discuss Young M.C.'s album acknowledgements and critique listener feedback regarding their commentary on homosexuality.
